title: Apache Log4j2 JNDI lookup remote code execution (Log4Shell)
description: Apache Log4j2 evaluates lookup expressions inside logged strings, and the directory-service lookup will fetch and deserialise a remote object. Any input that reaches a log statement therefore becomes a remote code execution path, including HTTP headers, user agents and form fields. The vulnerability was catastrophic in practice because Log4j2 is a transitive dependency of a very large fraction of Java software, so most affected organisations did not know they shipped it.
remediation: Upgrade Log4j2 to a patched release. Where upgrade is blocked, remove the lookup class from the deployed archive; configuration-only mitigations proved incomplete across versions. Inventory transitively, not from direct dependency manifests.

title: Apache Log4j2 incomplete fix allows denial of service and information leak
description: The first Log4j2 fix was incomplete for non-default configurations using a context lookup in the message pattern, leaving an exploitable path for information disclosure and denial of service. Its significance is procedural: organisations that had already declared themselves remediated had to repeat the whole inventory exercise days later.
remediation: Upgrade again to the later patched release rather than relying on the first patch. Treat a vendor's first advisory revision as provisional during an active mass-exploitation event.

title: Spring Framework data binding remote code execution (Spring4Shell)
description: Spring's request-parameter data binding could be steered to reach class-loader properties, which on a servlet container deployment allowed an attacker to write a file into the web root and obtain remote code execution. Exploitation depended on the deployment shape, which made asset inventory rather than version number the deciding factor for exposure.
remediation: Upgrade the framework. Where that is not immediate, restrict disallowed binding fields globally. Determine exposure from how the application is packaged and deployed, not from the dependency version alone.

title: XZ Utils upstream backdoor in liblzma affecting SSH authentication
description: A maintainer account that had built trust over years introduced obfuscated malicious code into the XZ release tarballs, hidden in test fixtures and activated only by the build scripts rather than present in the source repository. The payload hooked authentication in processes linked against the compression library, creating a pre-authentication remote access path on affected distributions. It is the clearest published example of a supply-chain compromise that no version-based scanner would have flagged, because the version was legitimate and the signature was valid.
remediation: Downgrade or upgrade to an unaffected release. Beyond the single fix, the lesson is that release artifacts must be reproducible from source and that maintainer-trust changes deserve the same review as code changes.

title: Apache Struts 2 multipart parser Content-Type remote code execution
description: A crafted Content-Type header was evaluated as an expression by the Struts multipart parser, giving unauthenticated remote code execution against any exposed endpoint. It is the vulnerability behind one of the largest consumer-data breaches on record, where the root cause was not the vulnerability itself but a patch that was available for months and an asset inventory that did not know where the framework was deployed.
remediation: Upgrade Struts. The durable control is an inventory that can answer which internet-facing services embed a given library within hours rather than weeks.

title: Remote Desktop Services pre-authentication remote code execution (BlueKeep)
description: A use-after-free in the remote desktop service allowed unauthenticated remote code execution with no user interaction, making it wormable across any network where the service was reachable. Exposure was driven almost entirely by remote-desktop ports published to the internet or left open flat across internal segments.
remediation: Patch, and separately remove direct exposure of remote desktop from the internet. Network-level authentication reduces but does not eliminate the pre-authentication surface.

title: Windows SMBv1 remote code execution (EternalBlue)
description: A flaw in the first version of the Windows file-sharing protocol allowed remote code execution against an exposed service, and was weaponised into self-propagating malware that caused two of the most damaging incidents on record. Internal spread was possible because the protocol was permitted host-to-host across flat networks.
remediation: Patch and disable the legacy protocol version entirely. East-west segmentation is the control that limits the damage when the next equivalent flaw appears.

title: Netlogon elevation of privilege via cryptographic flaw (Zerologon)
description: A flaw in the initialisation vector handling of the domain authentication protocol allowed an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a domain controller to set the controller's own machine account password, yielding immediate domain administrator equivalence. Any foothold on the internal network that could reach a domain controller was therefore a full domain compromise.
remediation: Patch domain controllers and then enforce the secure channel mode rather than leaving the compatibility period open. Monitor for machine-account password changes originating from non-controller sources.

title: Windows Print Spooler remote code execution (PrintNightmare)
description: The print service allowed an authenticated user to load a driver from a remote path, executing code with system privileges locally or on a remote host. Because the service runs by default on servers including domain controllers, it turned any domain user credential into a privilege-escalation and lateral-movement primitive.
remediation: Patch, restrict driver installation to administrators, and disable the spooler service wherever printing is not required, particularly on domain controllers.

title: Microsoft Exchange server-side request forgery (ProxyLogon)
description: A server-side request forgery in the client-access layer allowed an unauthenticated attacker to authenticate as the server itself, and chained with a write primitive it produced remote code execution. Mass exploitation dropped web shells on tens of thousands of servers within days of disclosure, including on servers patched shortly afterwards, which made web-shell hunting rather than patch status the necessary response.
remediation: Patch and then hunt: assume compromise for any server that was exposed before patching, and search web-accessible directories for unexpected files and mail-export activity.

title: Microsoft Exchange pre-authentication remote code execution (ProxyShell)
description: A path-confusion flaw in the mail server's request routing allowed unauthenticated access to privileged endpoints, which chained with two further flaws into remote code execution and mailbox export. It was widely used for initial access by ransomware operators through the second half of that year.
remediation: Patch to the current cumulative update. Exposure is decided by the published client-access surface, so removing direct internet exposure of management endpoints is the structural fix.

title: Microsoft Exchange server-side request forgery chain (ProxyNotShell)
description: An authenticated server-side request forgery that chains with a second flaw to reach remote code execution on the mail server. The interim mitigation rules published by the vendor were bypassed within days, which is a recurring pattern worth planning for: a request-pattern mitigation buys time, not safety.
remediation: Patch rather than relying on the published request-rewrite mitigations, and verify that the mitigation is still effective if patching must be deferred.

title: Citrix NetScaler session token leak (CitrixBleed)
description: A buffer over-read in the appliance leaked valid session tokens to an unauthenticated attacker, allowing session hijacking that bypassed both password and multi-factor authentication. Critically, patching alone did not help: sessions established before the patch remained valid and were used for access afterwards.
remediation: Patch and then terminate all existing sessions. This is the canonical example of why remediation for token-leak vulnerabilities must include session invalidation, not only the fix.

title: MOVEit Transfer SQL injection leading to remote code execution
description: A SQL injection in a managed file-transfer appliance allowed deployment of a web shell and mass theft of the data held for transfer. One vulnerability in one product produced data-breach notifications across thousands of downstream organisations, most of which had no direct relationship with the vendor, which is the defining property of third-party risk.
remediation: Patch and assume data exposure for any instance reachable before the fix. Managed file-transfer appliances aggregate other organisations' data and should be treated as high-value assets with their own monitoring.

title: Citrix ADC and Gateway directory traversal to remote code execution
description: A path-traversal flaw in the appliance's web interface allowed unauthenticated attackers to write and execute code. Exploitation began before patches were available for all versions, and compromised appliances frequently retained implants after the eventual patch.
remediation: Patch and then inspect the appliance filesystem and any persistence locations. Perimeter appliances rarely carry endpoint agents, so post-patch inspection is the only verification available.

title: Pulse Connect Secure arbitrary file read
description: An unauthenticated path-traversal read on a VPN appliance exposed session files containing plaintext credentials, which were then reused for ordinary VPN logins. The resulting access looked entirely legitimate, so detection required credential-reuse analysis rather than exploit detection.
remediation: Patch and force a credential reset for every account that had used the appliance, since the stolen credentials survive the patch.

title: FortiOS SSL VPN web portal path traversal
description: A path-traversal flaw in the VPN web portal allowed unauthenticated retrieval of session files including credentials. Lists of credentials harvested from unpatched devices circulated publicly for years afterwards and were still producing intrusions long after the patch was available.
remediation: Patch and rotate all VPN credentials. Assume that any credential present on an exposed unpatched device is public.

title: FortiOS SSL VPN heap buffer overflow pre-authentication remote code execution
description: A heap overflow in the VPN daemon gave unauthenticated remote code execution on the appliance, and observed exploitation included implants that patched the device's own logging functions to suppress evidence.
remediation: Patch and verify device integrity against vendor-provided checks; an appliance that can be made to lie in its own logs cannot be cleared on the basis of those logs.

title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect command injection
description: A command injection in the VPN feature of a firewall operating system allowed unauthenticated remote code execution as root on the device that enforces the perimeter. Exploitation was observed before public disclosure, and the initial telemetry guidance changed several times during the response.
remediation: Patch, then examine device logs and filesystem for the vendor-documented artifacts. Treat perimeter devices as in-scope for incident response rather than as infrastructure.

title: F5 BIG-IP iControl REST authentication bypass
description: A header-handling flaw allowed unauthenticated access to the management interface's command endpoints, which execute with root privileges. Exploitation required a single crafted request and was automated within a day of disclosure.
remediation: Patch and, independently of patching, remove the management interface from any network that does not strictly require it.

title: F5 BIG-IP Traffic Management UI remote code execution
description: A path-traversal flaw in the appliance's configuration interface permitted unauthenticated remote code execution. Like most appliance management flaws, it was only exploitable where the interface was reachable, which is a configuration decision rather than a software defect.
remediation: Patch, and restrict the configuration interface to a dedicated administrative network rather than relying on the patch alone. Every appliance management-plane flaw in this corpus is only exploitable where the interface is reachable, which makes reachability the control that generalises across all of them.

title: Atlassian Confluence OGNL injection remote code execution
description: An expression-language injection in a URL path allowed unauthenticated remote code execution on the wiki server. Wiki servers are high-value beyond their own compromise because they commonly hold credentials, runbooks and network diagrams.
remediation: Patch and then review the content the server held: a compromised knowledge base is a credential-exposure incident as well as a server incident.

title: VMware vCenter Server vSphere Client file upload remote code execution
description: An unauthenticated file upload in a vCenter plug-in endpoint permitted remote code execution on the host that controls the virtualisation estate. Compromise of the management plane grants access to every guest it manages, including ones with no other exposure.
remediation: Patch, and treat virtualisation management as a tier-zero asset with its own network segment and administrative accounts.

title: VMware vCenter Server analytics service arbitrary file upload
description: An arbitrary file upload in the telemetry service of the virtualisation management server allowed unauthenticated remote code execution. It was exploited in campaigns that deployed encryption directly against virtualisation hosts, which encrypts many guests at once and bypasses per-guest endpoint controls.
remediation: Patch and restrict management-plane access. Hypervisor-level encryption is fast and hard to detect from inside guests, so management-plane exposure deserves disproportionate attention.

title: Cisco IOS XE web UI privilege escalation to full administrator
description: An unauthenticated flaw in the device web interface allowed creation of a local administrator account on network devices, followed in observed activity by installation of a configuration-persisting implant. Tens of thousands of internet-reachable devices were affected within days.
remediation: Patch, disable the web interface where it is not needed, and audit local accounts on network devices. Network devices are frequently outside both the patch cycle and the monitoring footprint, which is what made this campaign so effective.

title: ConnectWise ScreenConnect authentication bypass
description: A path-handling flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker to re-run the setup wizard on a remote-management server and create an administrator account, gaining control of every endpoint the server managed. Because the tool is the managed service provider's own remote-access channel, one server compromise propagated to all downstream customers.
remediation: Patch immediately and audit administrator accounts on the management server. Remote-management platforms concentrate trust and should be treated as the highest-value asset a service provider operates.

title: Barracuda Email Security Gateway command injection in attachment screening
description: A command injection in the archive-handling path of an email security appliance gave remote code execution triggered simply by sending a crafted message. Exploitation preceded discovery by months, and the vendor ultimately recommended physical replacement of compromised appliances rather than patching.
remediation: Follow the vendor's replacement guidance. The general lesson is that security appliances parse hostile input by design and must be monitored as attack surface rather than trusted as controls.

title: Citrix NetScaler unauthenticated remote code execution
description: A code-injection flaw permitted unauthenticated remote code execution on the appliance and was used to place web shells on critical-infrastructure networks before public disclosure.
remediation: Patch and inspect for web shells and configuration changes; appliance compromise commonly outlives the patch.

title: Oracle WebLogic Server console authentication bypass to remote code execution
description: A path-normalisation flaw allowed unauthenticated access to the administration console, which then permits code execution. Exploitation was automated by cryptomining operators within days, making it a common source of long-lived low-severity-looking compromises.
remediation: Patch, and never expose the administration console beyond a dedicated administrative network. Cryptomining operators automate these within days of disclosure, so an exposed console tends to produce a long-lived, low-noise compromise that is discovered only when someone audits billing or CPU.

title: Drupal core form API remote code execution (Drupalgeddon2)
description: Insufficient sanitisation of nested form elements allowed unauthenticated remote code execution against a content management system. Mass scanning began within hours of the advisory, and unmaintained sites remained exploitable for years.
remediation: Patch or decommission. Content management systems without an owner are a recurring source of long-term footholds and should be inventoried explicitly.

title: Laravel Ignition debug page remote code execution
description: A development error-page component allowed file writes that led to remote code execution when an application was deployed with debug mode enabled. The vulnerability is in the component; the exposure is entirely caused by shipping a development configuration to production.
remediation: Patch, and separately enforce that debug modes cannot be enabled in production through deployment configuration checks.

title: OpenSSL heartbeat extension information disclosure (Heartbleed)
description: A missing bounds check in a transport-security extension allowed an attacker to read adjacent process memory, exposing private keys, session material and credentials with no trace in application logs. Remediation required key rotation and certificate reissuance in addition to patching.
remediation: Patch, reissue certificates, and rotate every credential that could have been resident in the process. A memory-disclosure flaw is a credential-exposure incident, not only a patching task.

title: GNU Bash environment variable function definition command injection (Shellshock)
description: Bash evaluated trailing commands in function definitions passed through environment variables, so any service that copied attacker-controlled input into the environment before invoking a shell became a remote code execution path. The affected surface was unusually hard to enumerate because it depended on how each service invoked shells.
remediation: Patch the shell. Architecturally, the lesson is to avoid passing untrusted input through the environment into shell invocations at all.

title: Linux kernel copy-on-write race condition local privilege escalation (Dirty COW)
description: A race in the kernel's copy-on-write handling allowed an unprivileged local user to write to read-only memory mappings and thereby gain root. It converts any code-execution foothold, including a web shell running as an unprivileged service account, into full host compromise.
remediation: Patch the kernel. Where kernel updates lag, the compensating control is limiting what can execute as the service account in the first place.

title: polkit pkexec local privilege escalation (PwnKit)
description: Incorrect argument handling in a setuid helper present by default on most Linux distributions allowed reliable local privilege escalation to root. Its reliability and ubiquity made it the default escalation step in Linux intrusions for a long period.
remediation: Patch the helper package, or remove the setuid bit as an interim measure on hosts where the helper is not used.

title: Linux kernel pipe buffer flag handling local privilege escalation (Dirty Pipe)
description: Uninitialised pipe buffer flags allowed an unprivileged user to overwrite arbitrary read-only files, including system binaries and credential files, giving straightforward root escalation and container escape in some configurations.
remediation: Patch the kernel; container platforms sharing a host kernel must be patched at the host level regardless of image contents.

title: sudo heap-based buffer overflow local privilege escalation (Baron Samedit)
description: A heap overflow reachable through a specific invocation mode allowed any local user, including users with no sudo rights at all, to gain root. It had been present for roughly a decade before discovery.
remediation: Patch sudo. The long dormancy is a reminder that the age of a component is not evidence of its safety.

title: sudo user identifier restriction bypass
description: A user permitted to run commands as any user except root could bypass the restriction with a crafted user identifier, executing as root anyway. Only configurations using explicit negation were affected, which made exposure a matter of reading policy files rather than versions.
remediation: Patch, and prefer allowlists over exclusion rules in privilege-delegation policy, since exclusion logic is where these bypasses live.

title: WinRAR archive extension spoofing leading to code execution
description: A crafted archive could cause a benign-looking file selection to execute a script from a same-named directory, so a user opening what appeared to be a document ran code instead. It was used in targeted campaigns against traders and later adopted by several intrusion sets.
remediation: Update the archive utility and treat archive attachments as executable content in mail policy.

title: HTTP/2 stream reset request cancellation denial of service (Rapid Reset)
description: Rapid creation and cancellation of protocol streams allowed a single connection to force large amounts of server-side work, producing record-scale denial of service with modest client resources. The flaw is in the protocol's design margin rather than in one implementation, so every implementation needed its own mitigation.
remediation: Apply implementation-specific patches and configure stream-reset rate limits. A protocol-level asymmetry cannot be fixed by capacity alone.

title: OpenSSL 3.0 punycode decoder buffer overflow in certificate verification
description: A stack overflow in the internationalised-name decoder was reachable during certificate verification, affecting servers that verify client certificates and clients connecting to hostile servers. Pre-announced as critical and downgraded on release, it became a useful case study in inventory readiness: most organisations could not answer which services used the affected major version.
remediation: Patch the library. Independently, maintain the ability to answer which deployed services link which version of a core cryptographic library within hours.

title: Microsoft Exchange static cryptographic key allows authenticated remote code execution
description: Mail servers shipped with a fixed cryptographic validation key, so any authenticated user could forge a serialised payload and execute code with elevated privileges on the server. A single stolen mailbox credential was therefore enough for server compromise.
remediation: Patch, which generates a unique key per installation. Treat any authenticated code-execution flaw on a mail server as reachable, since mailbox credentials are the most commonly stolen credential type.

title: libvpx VP8 encoding heap buffer overflow
description: A heap overflow in a widely embedded video codec was exploitable through content rendering, and was observed in commercial spyware delivery chains. The dependency is embedded in browsers, messaging clients and application runtimes, so patching required each embedder to ship an update.
remediation: Update every application that embeds the codec rather than only the operating system, and inventory embedded media libraries as dependencies in their own right.

title: Apache HTTP Server path traversal via path normalisation flaw
description: A flaw in path normalisation allowed traversal outside the document root, and where scripting handlers were enabled for the target path it extended to remote code execution. The fix for the first advisory was incomplete and required a second release.
remediation: Upgrade past both advisories and verify the traversal is closed by request rather than by version string alone.

title: event-stream npm package hijacked to steal cryptocurrency wallets
description: A volunteer who offered to take over maintenance of a popular but unmaintained npm package added a new dependency, then published malicious code into that dependency rather than the package itself. The payload was encrypted and only activated inside a specific downstream application, targeting cryptocurrency wallet keys. It is the reference case for maintainer-handover risk and for why transitive dependencies need the same scrutiny as direct ones.
remediation: Pin and audit transitive dependencies, review maintainer changes on critical packages, and prefer lockfile-enforced installs in continuous integration so a new transitive dependency cannot appear silently.

title: ua-parser-js npm account takeover ships cryptominer and credential stealer
description: An attacker took over the maintainer's npm account and published releases containing a cryptominer and a credential stealer. The package had millions of weekly downloads, so the malicious versions were installed widely within the few hours before removal, including by automated builds that resolved the newest version.
remediation: Require multi-factor authentication for publishers, pin exact versions in lockfiles, and delay adopting brand-new releases of critical dependencies in automated pipelines.

title: colors and faker npm packages sabotaged by their own maintainer
description: The maintainer of two very widely used npm packages deliberately published versions containing an infinite loop, breaking builds and running applications across thousands of projects. No attacker was involved, which is the point: availability risk in a dependency includes the maintainer's own intent and circumstances.
remediation: Pin versions and vendor or mirror critical dependencies so that an upstream publish cannot break a running deployment. Dependency risk assessment must cover maintainer sustainability, not only vulnerability counts.

title: PyTorch nightly dependency confusion via torchtriton package on PyPI
description: An attacker registered on the public package index a name that a machine-learning framework's nightly builds expected to resolve from its own index. The default resolver preferred the public package, and the malicious version exfiltrated environment details, host information and file contents from developer and build machines.
remediation: Configure package resolvers to never fall back from a private index to a public one for internally named packages, and claim internal names defensively on public registries.

title: 3CX desktop application signed installer backdoored through upstream vendor compromise
description: A telephony vendor's build environment was compromised and its signed desktop installer shipped with a backdoor to customers through the normal update channel. The vendor's own compromise was itself traced to a malicious package installed by an employee, making this a documented case of a supply-chain attack propagating through two vendors before reaching victims.
remediation: Behavioural monitoring of vendor binaries, because signature validation passes by construction. Cascading exposure means vendor risk assessment has to extend past the direct supplier.

title: SolarWinds Orion build pipeline compromise distributes SUNBURST backdoor
description: Adversaries modified the build process of a network-monitoring platform so that signed updates contained a backdoor, which then selected high-value victims and moved on into cloud identity infrastructure. The intrusion persisted for months and reframed supply-chain compromise from a theoretical risk into a board-level concern.
remediation: Reproducible builds and build-environment isolation on the vendor side; on the customer side, egress control and behavioural baselining for management software, which has broad credentials and broad network reach by design.

title: Codecov bash uploader modified to exfiltrate continuous integration secrets
description: An attacker modified a widely used coverage-upload script so that every build running it sent its environment variables to an external host. Because build environments hold deployment credentials, cloud keys and signing material, a single script produced credential exposure across many unrelated organisations.
remediation: Verify checksums of scripts fetched at build time, scope build credentials tightly, and rotate any secret that was present in an environment where a compromised build tool ran.

title: node-ipc npm package adds destructive geo-targeted payload
description: The maintainer of a transitively popular npm package published versions that overwrote files on machines whose network location resolved to particular countries. It demonstrated that a dependency can carry a destructive payload with no attacker involvement and no vulnerability in the conventional sense.
remediation: Pin transitive dependencies through lockfiles, and include destructive-behaviour scanning in dependency review rather than relying only on advisory databases.

title: Multi-year social engineering of an open-source maintainer preceding the XZ backdoor
description: Before any code was modified, the actor behind the XZ compromise spent years building a credible contributor reputation and applying pressure on an overloaded single maintainer until commit rights were granted. The technical payload was the last step of a human-trust attack, which is why it is recorded separately from the vulnerability identifier.
remediation: For consumers: prefer dependencies with multiple active maintainers, and treat single-maintainer critical dependencies as a tracked risk with an owner. For projects: require multi-party review for release tooling and build scripts, not only for source code.
